fact: Uganda's Constitutional Court struck down Sections 11, 23, 26, 27, 28 and 29 of the Computer Misuse Act and Sections 162 and 163 of the Penal Code Act (criminal libel), leaving the rest of the Act standing; the document gives no ruling day, so the published date is used.

Nilepost says Uganda's cyber-offence framework is anchored in the Computer Misuse Act, 2011 as amended by the Computer Misuse (Amendment) Act, 2022, with some offences carrying up to 10 years in prison.

Kampala Metropolitan Police arrested and hold three men, Ronald Mayiga, Swaibu Kakaire and Mark Mugoya, over alleged fake news and unlawful obtaining or disclosure of personal data on social media, in an investigation the report places under the Computer Misuse Act; charges were not disclosed and the incidents date to July 2026.

The joint UPR submission treats the Computer Misuse Act, Cap 96 as existing law, citing the Computer Misuse (Amendment) Act, 2022 and a March 2026 Constitutional Court decision on it, and urges repeal or amendment of sections 24 and 25.
